findings.title: The sibling-subdomain check treats unrelated domains under a multi-part public suffix as the same site.
findings.body: This branch drops the first label of each host and compares the rest. Suppose the instance is `forum.co.uk` and a user's website is `http://evil.co.uk/some/path`. Both hosts have 3 labels, and both reduce to `co.uk`, so the profile shows `evil.co.uk/some/path` as if it were on the instance's own domain. The same happens with other multi-part suffixes such as `com.au` or `github.io`. To fix this, compare registrable domains using a public-suffix-aware check. Alternatively, only treat hosts as related when one is the other or a subdomain of it.

findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the `?`, so the serializer never calls it.
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only calls conditional-inclusion hooks named `include_<attr>?`. Because this method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, it is dead code. As a result, `website_name` is always serialized, as `null` for users with no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, as the sibling `include_card_image_badge_id?` does.
